blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The people of Israel had finally left Egypt. Picture them camped beside the sea: mothers with babies on their hips, old men leaning on walking sticks, children asleep on bundles. Behind them were the years they had served in Egypt. In front of them was water as far as they could see.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then Pharaoh changed his mind. He wanted his workers back. He gathered his chariots and his horsemen and went after them.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Someone looked back and saw the dust rising on the road. The people were terribly afraid. They cried out to the LORD, and then they turned on Moses.

verses.text: And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to carry us forth out of Egypt?

segments.speaker: israelites
segments.text: Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to carry us forth out of Egypt?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Fear can do that. It can make the old hard life look safe, simply because it is familiar. But Moses did not answer their fear with more fear.

verses.text: And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Moses said unto the people,

segments.speaker: moses
segments.text: Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.

verses.text: The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

segments.speaker: moses
segments.text: The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Stand still, he told them. Not because there was nothing to do. Because this part was not theirs to do. Then the LORD told Moses to have the people go forward, and to lift his rod over the water.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Night came on. The angel of God, who had gone ahead of the camp, moved behind it, and the pillar of cloud moved with him. It stood between Israel and Egypt. On the Egyptian side it was cloud and darkness. On Israel's side it gave light all night long. The same cloud was darkness to one camp and light to the other.

verses.text: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

verses.text: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Imagine walking that path. Dry ground under your feet where fish had been swimming that morning. Water standing like walls on your right and on your left. Families walking together through the night.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The Egyptians followed them into the sea. Their chariot wheels came off, and they could barely drive. In the morning Moses stretched out his hand again, and the water returned to its place. Israel stood safe on the far shore.

verses.text: And Israel saw that great work which the LORD did upon the Egyptians: and the people feared the LORD, and believed the LORD, and his servant Moses.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Israel saw that great work which the LORD did upon the Egyptians: and the people feared the LORD, and believed the LORD, and his servant Moses.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Notice what the people learned that night. Not that they were strong, and not that Moses was clever. They saw what the LORD had done, and they trusted him. They could not see a way through the water. The story tells us who made one.

pastor.note: Faithful to Exodus 14; the Egyptians' end is told plainly without gloating; credit stays with the LORD.

cultural.note: Families and elders shown with dignity; no slavery imagery beyond what the text says.
